subtype: Approach: looking far ahead where he wants to go [Revision]
passage: The lane behind the market was narrow, and the light was almost gone. Siddharth wobbled forward, saw the wall at the corner, and steered straight into it. The bell on the handlebar rang out. Ramesh ran over. "You hit the wall because you stared at it. Now aim your eyes at the streetlight down the lane." Siddharth rubbed his elbow, and looked up. The streetlight glowed a long way off. He pushed off and pedalled. The handlebars turned slowly, and the cycle drifted along the middle of the lane. He reached the streetlight without touching anything.

qa.q: What did Ramesh tell Siddharth to look at?
qa.a: Ramesh told Siddharth to look at the streetlight down the lane.

qa.q: What might Siddharth have felt after he crashed into the wall?
qa.a: Siddharth was probably sore and embarrassed, shown by rubbing his elbow, but willing to try again.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Siddharth use to get better, and why?
qa.a: Siddharth could practise in a wide, open space in daylight before returning to the lane. More room gives more time to learn steering.

qa.q: How might Ramesh see the second attempt?
qa.a: Ramesh ran over and gave the advice, so Ramesh likely feels relieved and glad to see the tip work as the cycle drifts along the middle of the lane.

grounding: After crashing into a wall, a boy is told to look at the far end of the lane and finds his hands steer smoothly toward where his eyes point.

subtype: Approach: looking far ahead where he wants to go [Revision]
passage:
Farhan's cycle slammed into the housing society's compound wall for the second time that afternoon. He sat on the ground, rubbing his elbow and glaring at the bricks. Vasudha, the older girl from B-wing who rode every evening, leaned over the railing. "Where were you looking?"
"At the wall. So I wouldn't hit it."
"Don't. See the green gate at the end of the lane? Look only at that."
Farhan grumbled but climbed back on. He fixed his eyes on the green gate. The handle seemed to turn by itself, in small gentle corrections instead of jerks. He reached the gate without once touching the wall, then turned round and picked the mango tree at the other end.

qa.q: What was Farhan looking at when he hit the wall?
qa.a: He was looking at the wall, so he wouldn't hit it.

qa.q: How was Farhan feeling while he rubbed his elbow and glared at the bricks?
qa.a: He was sore and annoyed, frustrated that the wall kept winning.

qa.q: What would you advise Farhan if he starts drifting again on a new lane?
qa.a: Pick a clear target far ahead, like the mango tree, and keep the eyes there instead of on anything to avoid.

qa.q: How does the lesson look to Vasudha?
qa.a: Vasudha has learned it herself and can see his mistake, so it is easy for her and she is probably pleased when it works.

grounding: It shows a boy who crashes into a wall and, told to look far ahead, steers smoothly toward where he looks.

subtype: Approach: looking far ahead where he wants to go [Revision]
passage:
"Ow! That's the third time!"
"Hrithik, let me see the knee. Okay, just a scrape."
"The wall keeps jumping at me, Sahil bhaiya."
"Walls don't jump. Where were your eyes?"
"On the wall! I was watching it so I'd miss it."
"And you went straight into it. See the water tank at the far corner of the terrace?"
"The blue one?"
"Stare at that. Not the wall, not your wheel. Only the tank."
"And if I crash?"
"Then I'm wrong and you can laugh at me."
Hrithik pushed off, eyes on the tank.
"Bhaiya! I didn't even turn the handle. It just went there."
"Your hands follow your eyes. Now pick the door and ride back."

qa.q: What did Sahil tell Hrithik to stare at?
qa.a: He told him to stare at the blue water tank at the far corner of the terrace.

qa.q: How did Hrithik feel when he said the wall keeps jumping at him?
qa.a: He felt frustrated and a bit sore after three crashes, and blamed the wall.

qa.q: What other approach might help Hrithik on a narrow terrace, and why?
qa.a: Riding slowly between two slippers set on the floor, eyes on the far one, would give him an easy target and less to be scared of.

qa.q: What is it like for Sahil when the tip works?
qa.a: Sahil feels proud and relieved that his advice worked, and happy to give Hrithik the next target.

grounding: It shows a boy who crashed into a wall learning to look at a far point so his steering follows his eyes.
